Lysidinum.



Ethylene-Ethenyl-diamine. Methylglycoxalidine (Merck). Trituration.
        Solution.



Clinical. ─   Gout. Lithiasis. Oxaluria. Uric acid
        diathesis.



Characteristics. ─     Lysidin  .
        occurs in red-white crystals. The solution is a thick pinkish liquid. Clifford Mitchel (  H. W  ., xxxiii. 277) has given the 50 per cent. solution in
        ten-drop doses well diluted in aerated water, thrice daily, in two cases of oxaluria, one
        recent in a young man, one in an old man and of long standing. In the second case the
        distressing lumbar pain was removed by a few doses though it had persisted for a number of
        days.



Relations. ─     Compare:
        Nitro-mur. ac., Oxal. ac., Sars., Urotrop.
